articles.title: Introducing the Grid Protectors Program
articles.excerpt: OpenAI’s Grid Protectors Program will work with utilities to help future compute campuses support grid reliability and protect consumer electricity costs.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/grid-protectors-program/ Today we’re launching the **Grid Protectors Program**, a national effort to support affordable, reliable electricity for families and businesses in the communities where we build.
Working with utilities, regulators and policymakers, we’ll develop arrangements for our future campuses to reduce electricity demand when the grid is under strain.
Whether it’s heating homes during a northern cold snap or running air conditioning through a southern heat wave, families need reliable electricity.
Our goal is to make campus flexibility a resource that utilities can call on when communities need it most.

With U.S. data center capacity projected to exceed 100 gigawatts by 2030, we have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to strengthen the electric grid by building campuses that can adjust their power use when communities need it most.

articles.title: LifeVal
articles.excerpt: Introducing LifeVal, a benchmark measuring how well AI helps people complete everyday tasks, from finding childcare to managing finances and government paperwork.
details: For the more than one billion people who currently use ChatGPT every week, we want to build AI that can help with the practical challenges of everyday life, like finding childcare, accessing government services, creating a budget, preparing for school, modifying recipes, ordering groceries, designing workout plans, and more.
When someone is looking for help making their life easier, they need more than advice or a chat response.
To be a truly helpful personal assistant, ChatGPT should be able to take actions that actually get things done.
To measure model performance over time on everyday tasks, we built an evaluation of tasks covering areas where users wanted the most help from AI and personal agents.
We used this evaluation to track and drive improvement in model performance on everyday tasks over the past year.

articles.title: Qodo builds context into AI code review with Codex
articles.excerpt: Qodo brings company knowledge and coding standards into Codex, helping developers catch P0 issues across repositories before opening a pull request.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/qodo-codex-plugin/ Qodo builds AI tools for code review and software quality, giving coding agents the organizational knowledge they need to understand the code they change.
Co-founder and CEO Itamar Friedman calls it “the coding agent’s best friend.” Qodo uses OpenAI models including GPT‑6 Astra to gather engineering knowledge, review code, and monitor software quality.
Its Codex plugin brings that context and review into developers’ coding sessions. > “We love OpenAI models.

We want the frontier, the best reasoning models, but also those that are really fast.” -Itamar Friedman, Co-founder and CEO, Qodo Finding P0 bugs across repositories with Codex Itamar describes customer environments that can span 10,000 or more repositories, where a local code change can break a downstream service, even if it looks correct on its own.
Qodo built a plugin in the Codex marketplace to address this.

articles.title: The Ecosystem is the Answer: Docker, the Blueprint Alliance, and the Importance of Collaboration in the Agentic Era
articles.excerpt: Docker is a founding member of the Blueprint Alliance, a 12-company reference architecture for securing AI agents, built around four governance questions.
details: In 2025, the average global Fortune 500 enterprise had fewer than 15 AI agents in use. Gartner expects that number to explode to more than 150,000 by 2028 . Only 13 percent of organizations think they have the right governance for today, and AI is evolving and moving faster than any other technology paradigm in our history.

Today, most security leaders face an agentic Sophie’s choice: allow AI adoption without the right controls and hope for the best, or block it and become the obstacle to a priority the business has already set (while adoption continues in the shadows, anyway).

But there is a third option, one in which organizations fully tap into the transformative power of agentic agents without having to live in fear of a catastrophic security failure. The good news is history has already shown how to get there.

Historically, technology adoption has followed a reliable pattern. A capability spreads, each vendor and team builds its own approach, the inconsistency becomes expensive and ineffective, leading the industry to agree to a shared baseline. Adoption then accelerates.

Take the credit card industry, for example. The big credit brands each ran their own security programs, and merchants had to satisfy every one. This was, of course, cumbersome for the vendors, but also for the customers, too. Every time a customer wanted to adopt a new technology, they had to manually build out security and adoption plans, adding significant adoption and procurement delays.

articles.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI
articles.excerpt: How OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend designed for the scale of development that Codex makes possible.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/scaling-git-at-openai/ Over the past year, the size and demands on our monorepo have increased at a staggering pace.
It was clear that we needed to revamp our source control system to scale to the level of concurrent work that Codex makes possible.
We built Pando, a new backend for Git repositories, without interrupting any engineering work or changing how our team uses Git.
Pando is designed to meet two ambitious goals: first, horizontally scalable writes, optimized for concurrent pushes to many branches.
And second, maximize read throughput, so clients can download data fast enough to fully saturate their available network bandwidth.

articles.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85%
articles.excerpt: Zone setting changes used to rebuild entire DNS zones, even ones with tens of millions of records. Here is how we built a planner that picks the smallest safe build, cutting full builds by 40%, peak memory by 85%, and halving build delay.
details: When I last wrote about our DNS propagation pipeline in 2022 , the Zone Builder received about 250 DNS record changes per second.
Today it receives about 700, nearly three times as many, plus about 100 other events, such as zone setting changes.
However, the number of events was never the real problem.
The problem was the kind of work some of those events needed, and how that work grows with the size of a zone.
Some zones now hold more than 20 million records, and we expect them to keep growing toward hundreds of millions.

articles.title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
articles.excerpt: Public traffic to private origins, with WAF, bot management, caching, and Workers, is now available to every customer with Cloudflare One connectivity.
details: Today, Cloudflare services for private origins is generally available. Point a proxied DNS record at a private IP, and Cloudflare reaches the origin over your existing Cloudflare One connection . Your origin stays private, while web application firewall ( WAF ), caching , bot management , and Workers work just as they do for public origins.

In June, we launched this capability in closed beta to address a problem we kept hearing from customers: Their internal APIs, AI agent backends, MCP servers, and operational tools weren’t built to face the Internet, but those services still need to accept requests from partners, customers, or agents over the Internet.
Before the beta, putting Cloudflare in front of these services meant exposing a public IP, opening a firewall port, or running cloudflared alongside the origin.

Those requirements often left private applications without the same protections and controls they used for public applications, including WAF, bot management, rate limiting, caching, traffic acceleration, rewrites, and Workers.
During the closed beta, eligible customers requested access through their account team. Today, we’re opening access beyond that beta group.

articles.title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
articles.excerpt: Cloudflare mitigated over 8,200 DDoS attacks per hour in Q3 2026 as attackers shifted to shorter, high-frequency strikes. Explore the latest threat data, including the collapse of CLDAP vectors and the impact of recent botnet takedowns.
details: Welcome to the 26th edition of Cloudflare's DDoS Threat Report.
This edition covers the third quarter of 2026 - July, August, and September - and returns the series to its quarterly cadence following the combined H1 2026 volume.

The analysis is produced by Cloudforce One , Cloudflare's Threat Intelligence organization, providing a comprehensive analysis of the evolving threat landscape of Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks based on data from the Cloudflare network .
Short-burst, low-bandwidth attacks lasting under 10 minutes and 1 Gbps surged by 208%.

Conversely, hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps plummeted by nearly 69% from Q2, possibly a reflection of law enforcement actions against four major Internet of Things (IoT) botnets earlier in the year.

articles.title: What took the Internet offline in Q3 2026
articles.excerpt: An examination of global Internet disruptions observed by Cloudflare Radar during the third quarter of 2026. This review analyzes how power failures, natural disasters, and government shutdowns impacted network connectivity and traffic.
details: The Internet can feel invisible when everything is working normally.
But when connectivity breaks, the many systems it depends upon become evident in an instant.
Because Cloudflare’s global network handles more than 20% of the web’s traffic, it offers a unique perspective of how Internet traffic is behaving.
When failures in infrastructure, power, policy, or security disrupt access to the Internet, Cloudflare Radar can observe the impact by monitoring traffic to our customers.
Each quarter, we review the disruptions detected and annotated on Radar, highlighting what happened, where it happened, and the broader conditions that shaped each event.

articles.title: Announcing the Workload Conformance Working Group
articles.excerpt: We are excited to announce that the Kubernetes community now has a Workload Conformance Working Group . The working group is writing a shared standard for how workloads behave at runtime on Kubernetes. To get it right, we need input from the people who build those workloads and from the people who run the…
details: Certified Kubernetes tests the cluster, and Kubernetes AI Conformance tests whether a cluster can run AI and ML workloads. Nothing comparable exists for the workloads themselves, so cluster operators still check each application by hand before routine maintenance or a Kubernetes upgrade.

The problems they find are familiar. A routine node drain is often how you discover that an application can't tolerate disruption. An upgrade can break an application that still depends on a removed API version . Others show up in day-to-day operation: workloads that ask for privileges they don't need, or reserve resources they never use.

Kubernetes already documents much of this, including security and handling disruptions . Even so, every cluster operator ends up repeating the same assessment, and application maintainers get the same questions from each environment they support. A common specification with repeatable tests would give both groups the same baseline to start from.
A specification of workload behavior for each Kubernetes minor version.
A method for testing each requirement against a running workload.

articles.title: Rewarding defenders with bigger bug bounties
articles.excerpt: OpenAI is raising Security Bug Bounty rewards and introducing report quality, loyalty, and priority campaign bonuses for independent security researchers.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/rewarding-defenders-with-bigger-bug-bounties/ We’re raising rewards in OpenAI’s Security Bug Bounty program to further encourage independent researchers to pursue vulnerabilities in OpenAI software that our testing may have missed.
We’re also introducing new incentives for researchers to earn more for higher quality vulnerability reports.
Independent security researchers play an essential role in protecting technology across the industry.

At OpenAI, incentivizing responsible disclosure is a core part of our security model, complementing our Defense Factory⁠ work, where our engineers use our models to find weaknesses, reproduce them, and test fixes.
Today’s updates are designed to encourage and empower researchers, and to continue building a collaborative, community-first security environment.

articles.title: Preparing our next security sprint to harden OpenAI
articles.excerpt: OpenAI is preparing its next internal security sprint with Cathedral Systems to test and strengthen its defenses using AI.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/preparing-our-next-security-sprint-to-harden-openai/ We’re planning our next internal security sprint at OpenAI, bringing new researchers and security partners together with our own teams to use our models to test and strengthen our systems.

We’re partnering with Cathedral, whose researchers will use OpenAI’s models alongside our teams to challenge our defenses, bringing differentiated expertise and approaches to finding weaknesses and helping us protect our platforms.
We’re also making improvements to ourSecurity Bug Bounty program including more than quadrupling our rewards for critical findings.
We want researchers to challenge our assumptions and help strengthen both our systems and the methods we use to defend them.
This is part of our ongoing effort to use AI to continuously find and fix weaknesses in our systems.

articles.title: OpenAI appoints Dan Driscoll as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization
articles.excerpt: OpenAI appoints Dan Driscoll to advise on responsible AI for national security modernization, cyber resilience, and collaboration with U.S. allies.
details: Final URL: https://openai.com/index/dan-driscoll-joins-openai/ Dan Driscoll will join OpenAI as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization, working with senior leadership and external partners to advise on how advanced AI can strengthen national and cyber security, with a particular focus on working with U.S. allies to advance its responsible use.

In this newly created role, Dan will work with OpenAI teams and leaders across governments, industry, academia, and allied institutions to advance practical modernization initiatives that support the buildout of democratic AI.
He will also help internal OpenAI teams understand the operational needs of global national security institutions.
Dan previously served as the 26th Secretary of the Army, overseeing the service’s operations, modernization, and resources.
He brings experience spanning military service, senior government leadership, and the private sector.

articles.title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
articles.excerpt: Four, just four: that’s the key to break into any unpatched connection on the Internet that is using eMudhra certificates. Here’s how we quickly patched Cloudflare, what evidence we can see of attempted exploitation, and how much of the rest of the Internet remains exposed.
details: On October 19, 2026, we learned about eMudhra’s eight shockingly weak keys: where eMudhra was trusted to pick a 115-digit number for their virtual combination lock protecting the Internet, they picked the number 4. Not even four digits, just the number 4. The other seven keys were similarly weak: 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237.

The next day, we wrote a blog post on the immediate action we took to mitigate this leak, and what customers needed to do on their end to stay secure. Now, we are sharing a more in-depth follow up on the evidence we’ve seen of exploitation, and the progress seen on visitors patching their systems.
A certificate authority (CA) with weak keys this serious is unprecedented, and the potential consequences are significant.

While there have been plenty of compromised certification authorities in the past (such as DigiNotar , TÜRKTRUST , and TrustWave ), access to their keys has always been contained to a degree; these incidents gave a limited set of attackers or organizations the ability to issue fraudulent certificates.
The eMudhra incident is fundamentally different; the affected intermediate private keys could be recovered almost instantly by anyone from the public certificates themselves.

articles.title: Game Off 2026: The theme is SHIFT
articles.excerpt: GitHub’s annual month-long game jam is back for its 14th year! This November, make a game inspired by the theme SHIFT. Change gears, swap perspectives, bend reality, or just press a certain key. The post Game Off 2026: The theme is SHIFT appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Game Off , GitHub's annual month-long game jam, returns for its 14th year this November. Thousands of developers have joined us over the years to make everything from polished platformers to wonderfully weird experiments.
Whether you're making your first game or your fiftieth, we'd love for you to join us.
Shift gears. Shift perspectives. Shift dimensions. Shift bits. Work the night shift. Or make a game where the only buttons are the Shift keys.
You have until December 1, 2026, at 13:37 PST to build and submit a game inspired by SHIFT. Strong or loose inspirations apply!
A change in position, direction, perspective, or reality.

articles.title: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
articles.excerpt: Today, we laid out our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive, end-to-end software delivery system in the world. The post GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
details: Our jobs as developers are changing. In a couple of years, we've gone from writing every line of code to working with AI assistants to orchestrating fleets of agents. But the goal hasn't changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters.

Today at GitHub Universe , we shared our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world. We introduced products that bring that vision to life and showed how we're rebuilding the infrastructure underneath it.
The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment.
A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system.
Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand.
